follow100Note: Tax added $0.76 back to every $100 because Qualcomm recorded a $78M tax benefit this quarter, not a tax bill. The spending rows add to $99.99 rather than exactly $100.00 because each row is rounded to two decimals.
footerNote: Qualcomm does not print a gross profit line; gross profit here is total revenues less cost of revenues, exactly as its statement of operations foots. Qualcomm guided Q1 FY27 revenue to $10.4B–$11.2B and reiterated a $5B fiscal 2027 Data Center revenue target. Non-GAAP figures it headlines (revenue $10,442M, EPS $2.17) exclude QSI, share-based compensation, the restructuring charge and the legal-settlement payment. Chart note: Qualcomm's tax line was a $78M benefit, not a bill, so the chart draws it as its own green 'Tax benefit' source flowing into net profit — it is not folded into any other line.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs a $2.89 loss a year ago

oneTimers: Restructuring and restructuring-related charges of $235M are the whole of the 'Other' operating-expense line this quarter; Qualcomm excludes them from non-GAAP results, along with $141M of acquisition-related charges spread across its cost lines.

GAAP revenue includes a $120M payment to a customer resulting from a recent legal settlement, recorded as unallocated revenue. That is why non-GAAP revenue of $10,442M is higher than GAAP revenue of $10,322M.

The year-ago quarter is a distorted comparison: in Q4 FY25 Qualcomm booked a $6,088M income tax expense (largely a valuation allowance on deferred tax assets) and a net loss of $3,117M. In fiscal 2026 it released that valuation allowance, a $5.7B tax benefit recorded earlier in the year.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $170M plus investment and other expense, net of $13M — a net $183M non-operating cost. Inside the investment results, QSI's strategic investments lost about $120M in the quarter after gains earlier in the year, partly offset by gains on deferred-compensation plan assets.

segments.name: QCT
segments.note: The chip business (Snapdragon and Dragonwing), down 8% YoY. Inside it: Handsets $5,137M (down 26%), Automotive $1,990M (up 89%, a record first $2B quarter) and IoT $1,888M (up 4%).

segments.name: QTL
segments.note: Patent licensing, down 7% YoY — and very profitable: earnings before tax of $918M, or 70% of its revenue.

segments.name: Other and reconciling items
segments.note: QSI, the strategic-investments arm, earned no revenue. Nonreportable segments (Data Center, QGOV and Modular) brought in $123M, less a $120M payment to a customer from a legal settlement recorded as unallocated revenue — a net $3M.

takeaways.text: Automotive revenue reached $1,990M — Qualcomm's first $2B automotive quarter — up 89% from a year ago. Together, Automotive and IoT grew 36% YoY and are carrying the business while handsets shrink.
takeaways.title: Cars are the growth engine

takeaways.text: Handset revenue fell to $5,137M, down 26% YoY, dragging QCT down 8% and total revenue down 8% to $10,322M. Qualcomm renewed long-term QTL license agreements with Apple, Huawei and Transsion during the quarter.
takeaways.title: Handsets pulled revenue down

takeaways.text: Net income was $1,251M, against a $3,117M net loss a year ago — that loss came from a $6,088M tax expense, not from operations. This quarter tax was actually a $78M benefit on $1,173M of pre-tax profit.
takeaways.title: Profit bounced back from last year's tax hit

verdict: Qualcomm's revenue fell 8% to $10.3B as handset chip sales dropped 26%, but automotive chips nearly doubled to a record $2.0B — and a $235M restructuring charge plus a $120M legal-settlement payment held GAAP profit to $1.25B.
